resources.string: Android only allows one active VPN at a time. Turning AppNetBlocker on will disconnect the other VPN.
Blocker service was stopped by the system
Your device stopped the VPN service in the background. Disable battery optimization and enable Always-on VPN in Settings for better reliability.
Another VPN took over or VPN access was removed in system settings. Toggle blocking on again to restore protection.
Android could not create the local VPN tunnel. Check that no conflicting VPN profile is locked and try again.
Auto-start on boot was blocked by Android
Android 14+ can restrict background service starts after reboot. Enable Always-on VPN in system VPN settings so Android starts AppNetBlocker automatically.
Android VPN rules apply per user profile. Blocking may not work for apps running inside a work profile, Dual Apps, or Secure Folder.
Work / dual profile — may not work
Enter an exact Android package name (for example, com.easybrain.killer.sudoku) to select and pin an app.
This package is not installed on this device.

This is a local VPN. No traffic is sent anywhere.\n\nAppNetBlocker uses Android\'s VpnService on your device to intercept traffic only from the apps you select and drop their packets locally. All other apps keep working normally, and AppNetBlocker does not request the internet permission.
Select at least one app first.
All apps unselected. Blocker turned off.

Recommended on Android 14 and 15. When enabled in system VPN settings, Android keeps AppNetBlocker active and restarts it after a reboot. Keep \"Block connections without VPN\" OFF so unselected apps still have internet.
Android and OEM power managers (Samsung, Xiaomi, Oppo, Huawei) can kill background services. Granting exemption prevents unexpected stops.
Try to restart blocking automatically after reboot if VPN permission was already granted. On Android 14+, Always-on VPN is more reliable if the OS restricts boot background starts.

AppNetBlocker creates a local-only VPN tunnel using VpnService.Builder.addAllowedApplication(). Only the apps you select enter the tunnel; their IPv4 and IPv6 packets are read and dropped locally without forwarding or external DNS. All other apps bypass the VPN.
